bullets: Erosion patterns on race-tracks change line choice from practice to race day — a critical but often overlooked factor in race strategy.
Speed comes from braking earlier and smoother, not from taking bigger risks — a counterintuitive principle validated across multiple teams using RockShox.
Tire pressure and casing choice matter more than minor suspension tweaks — the framing of equipment decisions reveals underlying tradeoffs.
Risk management in racing isn’t about avoiding crashes — it’s about choosing which crashes are survivable, a mindset shift that alters performance outcomes.
The second-order effect of smart risk management is visible in platform adoption — Cascadia Alliance shows how systems amplify or diminish real-world results.
Spoke & Wrench integration makes tradeoffs explicit — teams using it see clearer cause-and-effect in their performance decisions.
The most underrated piece of enduro racing is recognizing how erosion alters line selection — a dynamic that shapes every lap.
Adopting a single idea for two weeks enables iteration — real learning comes from sustained, practical application, not theory alone.
